$schema: Exam-legal bookmark set. Every `url` must be inside one of `allowed`; scripts/check-data.mjs enforces that. `when` is the symptom or task wording that should make you reach for the page — it is the label you scan, not the doc's own title.
policyNote: The Linux Foundation permits ONE extra browser tab, restricted to the domains listed in `allowed`. Verify that list against the Candidate Handbook and the 'Resources Allowed' page before your exam — it is revised with the curriculum.

allowed.note: The kubernetes GitHub org and its repositories

folders.name: 0 · First 60 seconds
folders.why: Open before task 1. Everything here answers 'what is the flag called' faster than a search does — but slower than `kubectl explain`, so use them only when explain has failed you.

items.title: kubectl quick reference
items.when: The alias/completion block, and every imperative one-liner. The single highest-value page in the set.

items.title: kubectl create — subcommands
items.when: "Can I generate this instead of writing YAML?" — the list of what `create` can produce.

items.title: API reference — object fields
items.when: An exact field name or its nesting, when `kubectl explain --recursive` is not enough.

items.title: kubectl for Docker users / command index
items.when: You know the verb but not the flag, and the quick reference did not have it.

folders.name: 1 · Troubleshooting — 30%
folders.why: The heaviest domain, and the one that does not yield to reading. These are ordered the way a broken cluster is diagnosed: cluster, then node, then Pod, then network.

items.title: Cluster is broken — where to look
items.when: Nodes NotReady, control-plane component down, API server unreachable.

items.title: Static Pod manifests (control plane)
items.when: apiserver/etcd/scheduler won't start — the manifest path and how the kubelet picks it up.

items.title: crictl — containers below kubectl
items.when: The API server itself is down and you need the container logs anyway.

items.title: kubelet config file
items.when: A kubelet flag or path is wrong and you need to know which file to fix.

items.title: Node status and conditions
items.when: Reading `describe node`: DiskPressure, MemoryPressure, what each condition means.

items.title: Application not running
items.when: Pending, CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff — the triage order.

items.title: Debug Pods
items.when: A Pod is Pending or restarting and `describe` has not told you why yet.

items.title: kubectl debug / ephemeral containers
items.when: The image has no shell, or you need to poke at a running Pod from inside.

items.title: Service has no endpoints
items.when: Service exists, `get endpoints` is empty — the selector/port checklist.

items.title: DNS resolution debugging
items.when: Name resolution fails inside Pods; CoreDNS Pods or config suspect.

items.title: metrics-server / kubectl top
items.when: `kubectl top` errors, or the task asks you to report resource usage.

items.title: Container logs and streams
items.when: "Write the output stream of container X to a file" — where the logs actually live.

items.title: System component logs
items.when: journalctl vs /var/log — which component logs where.

folders.name: 2 · Cluster architecture — 25%
folders.why: etcd and kubeadm are the two tasks people most often lose whole on. Both are procedural: the page is worth opening even when you think you remember the order.

items.title: etcd — BACK UP
items.when: `etcdctl snapshot save` with the three TLS flags. Do not type this from memory.

items.title: etcd — RESTORE
items.when: `snapshot restore --data-dir`, then repoint the static Pod manifest.

items.title: kubeadm upgrade — control plane
items.when: Drain → unhold → plan → apply → kubelet → restart → uncordon, in that order.

items.title: kubeadm upgrade — worker nodes
items.when: `kubeadm upgrade node` — the step people skip after upgrading the control plane.

items.title: Drain a node safely
items.when: `--ignore-daemonsets`, `--delete-emptydir-data`, and when drain hangs.

items.title: kubeadm join / create a cluster
items.when: Add a node; regenerate a join token; where admin.conf goes.

items.title: kubeadm token — new join command
items.when: The join token expired: `kubeadm token create --print-join-command`.

items.title: HA control-plane topologies
items.when: Stacked vs external etcd — the distinction a question can turn on.

items.title: kubeadm certificate renewal
items.when: Expired control-plane certs; `kubeadm certs check-expiration`.

items.title: RBAC — Role / RoleBinding YAML
items.when: verbs, apiGroups, resourceNames — the exact spec shape.

items.title: RBAC — imperative + auth can-i
items.when: `create role/rolebinding` flags, and how to prove the binding works.

items.title: ServiceAccount for a Pod
items.when: Bind a role to a ServiceAccount and attach it to a workload.

items.title: CertificateSigningRequest (user access)
items.when: "Create a user and grant it access" — CSR YAML, approve, build the kubeconfig.

items.title: kubeconfig — contexts and users
items.when: `set-credentials` / `set-context` when you must hand back a working kubeconfig.

items.title: CRDs — define a custom resource
items.when: Install or inspect a CRD; `kubectl get crd`, scope, versions.

items.title: Operator pattern
items.when: A question frames a controller-plus-CRD as an operator.

items.title: Extension interfaces — CNI / CSI / CRI
items.when: Which interface owns what; where a CNI config file lives.

items.title: Container runtimes (CRI setup)
items.when: cgroup driver, containerd config, the socket path.

folders.name: 3 · Services & networking — 20%
folders.why: Gateway API is the post-2025 addition most people have not practised. NetworkPolicy is the one YAML on the exam that is genuinely hard to produce cold.

items.title: NetworkPolicy — the resource
items.when: podSelector / ingress / egress / ports. Copy, then cut.

items.title: NetworkPolicy — default deny
items.when: "Deny all traffic except…" — the empty-selector policies.

items.title: NetworkPolicy — walkthrough
items.when: You want the worked example rather than the reference.

items.title: Service — types and ports
items.when: ClusterIP / NodePort / LoadBalancer; targetPort vs port vs nodePort.

items.title: Endpoints and EndpointSlices
items.when: Verifying a Service actually selected Pods.

items.title: Ingress — the resource
items.when: Path rules, pathType, backend service — the YAML to copy.

items.title: IngressClass
items.when: The Ingress is created but no controller picks it up.

items.title: Gateway API (Kubernetes docs)
items.when: GatewayClass → Gateway → HTTPRoute, on the allowed kubernetes.io domain.

items.title: Gateway API — official site
items.when: The upstream docs. Allowed for CKA only. Deep links move between releases — enter through the root.

items.title: Gateway API — guides
items.when: A worked HTTPRoute; simple gateway; traffic splitting.

items.title: DNS for Services and Pods
items.when: The FQDN form: svc.namespace.svc.cluster.local.

items.title: CoreDNS customisation
items.when: Editing the CoreDNS Corefile ConfigMap.

items.title: Connect applications with a Service
items.when: Expose a Deployment end to end, verified from a client Pod.

folders.name: 4 · Workloads & scheduling — 15%
folders.why: Most of this domain is imperative kubectl and should never cost you a page load. These are the exceptions — the spec blocks with nesting you will get wrong from memory.

items.title: Deployment — rollout and rollback
items.when: `rollout undo --to-revision`, `rollout history`, `rollout status`.

items.title: Deployment — update strategy
items.when: maxSurge / maxUnavailable placement in the spec.

items.title: ConfigMap into a Pod
items.when: envFrom vs valueFrom vs volume mount — all three shapes on one page.

items.title: Secrets with kubectl
items.when: `create secret generic --from-literal`, and reading one back.

items.title: Probes — liveness / readiness / startup
items.when: The probe block, including initialDelaySeconds and the exec form.

items.title: Requests and limits
items.when: resources: block; units for cpu and memory.

items.title: HPA — walkthrough
items.when: "Configure workload autoscaling" — `kubectl autoscale`, then verify.

items.title: HPA — how it decides
items.when: The v2 spec with metrics, if a target other than CPU is asked for.

items.title: Taints and tolerations
items.when: NoSchedule / PreferNoSchedule / NoExecute, and the toleration block.

items.title: nodeSelector and node affinity
items.when: required vs preferred — the nesting nobody remembers.

items.title: Scheduling reference
items.when: Pod affinity/anti-affinity and topologySpreadConstraints.

items.title: PodDisruptionBudget
items.when: minAvailable / maxUnavailable, usually paired with a drain task.

items.title: DaemonSet
items.when: One Pod per node, and why a drain needs --ignore-daemonsets.

items.title: CronJob and Job
items.when: schedule, restartPolicy, backoffLimit — `create cronjob` gets you most of it.

items.title: Init containers
items.when: A Pod must wait on something before its main container starts.

folders.name: 5 · Storage — 10%
folders.why: Ten percent, and almost always the same shape: make a PVC bind. The three conditions for binding are what the page is really for.

items.title: PV and PVC — binding lifecycle
items.when: The PVC is Pending: accessModes, size, storageClassName must all agree.

items.title: PV / PVC YAML to copy
items.when: A minimal volume spec you can edit down in seconds.

items.title: PV walkthrough (hostPath)
items.when: The full PV → PVC → Pod chain, which is the usual exam task.

items.title: StorageClass
items.when: provisioner, reclaimPolicy, volumeBindingMode.

items.title: Change the default StorageClass
items.when: The is-default-class annotation, exactly as spelled.

items.title: Dynamic provisioning
items.when: A PVC should create its PV rather than match an existing one.

items.title: Volume types
items.when: emptyDir, hostPath, configMap and secret volumes.

folders.name: 6 · Helm & Kustomize
folders.why: Added to the curriculum in the 2025 revision, and the most common gap in people who studied from older material. Helm's docs are a separate allowed domain.

items.title: Kustomize with kubectl
items.when: kustomization.yaml; `kubectl apply -k`; `kubectl kustomize` to preview.

items.title: Helm — using Helm
items.when: install / upgrade / rollback / uninstall and what each does.

items.title: helm install
items.when: `--set`, `-f values.yaml`, `--namespace --create-namespace`.

items.title: helm upgrade
items.when: `--install`, `--reuse-values`, and rolling a release forward.

items.title: helm repo add
items.when: Add and update a chart repository before installing from it.

items.title: helm template
items.when: "Show what this chart would apply" without touching the cluster.

items.title: Charts — values and structure
items.when: Where values.yaml sits and how overrides resolve.
